headline: Southborough boards advanced a draft 55-plus housing zoning proposal, transferred housing funds to earn interest, and planned trail expansion grants.
synopsis: The Affordable Housing Trust backed draft zoning rules allowing up to eight senior housing units per acre and moved approximately one million dollars into an interest-bearing savings program. The Trails Committee initiated partnership planning for a 2027 MassTrails grant of up to $100,000 while reviewing roadway crossing options on Route 30 and Central Street. Additionally, the Municipal Technology Committee examined outreach for the 2026 Resident Satisfaction Survey and tracked an upcoming town hall phone system transition.

highlights.title: Draft senior housing zoning bylaw advancement
highlights.why: The trust reached consensus on a draft bylaw removing the town-wide 7 percent cap on elderly housing units while establishing a two-acre minimum lot size and a 12.5 percent affordable unit mandate. Members plan to present the draft to the Planning Board, Zoning Board of Appeals, and Select Board.

highlights.title: Transfer of housing funds to interest-bearing program
highlights.why: The trust arranged to move roughly one million dollars from a zero-interest account into an insured savings program earning about 3.5 percent interest. The move is expected to yield approximately $35,000 annually for municipal housing efforts.

highlights.title: Outreach for 2027 MassTrails grant
highlights.why: The committee began preparations to apply for a state grant of up to $100,000 requiring a 20 percent match for trail development. Members plan to collaborate with Southborough and Framingham public schools to incorporate trail visits into science curricula.

highlights.title: Trail roadway crossings and parking coordination
highlights.why: Following Town Meeting funding approval, members discussed pursuing lower-cost crossing options with DPW and MassDOT rather than a quoted $600,000 to nearly $1 million intersection overhaul on Route 30. The committee also intends to approach Sanofi regarding public trail parking access.

highlights.title: Town phone system cutover and website planning
highlights.why: Municipal offices will migrate to a cloud-based phone system operating over Wi-Fi on November 13, eliminating on-premises equipment. Preliminary discussions are also underway with vendor CivicPlus for a municipal website redesign.
